summary.text: Earth's largest volcanic eruptions can reach far beyond the volcano, with regional or even global effects, some changing the climate and helping cause mass extinctions.
Eruptions come in two broad kinds: explosive ones that suddenly blast out rock and ash, and effusive ones that pour out lava more gently.
Gentle does not mean safe: Iceland's lava-pouring Laki eruption of 1783–1784 killed one fifth of the island's people.

items.prompt: A volcano oozes a steady stream of runny lava for months, with no big blasts. What kind of eruption is this?

options.label: An explosive eruption
An ash-cloud eruption
An effusive eruption
A pyroclastic eruption

items.explain: A relatively gentle, steady outpouring of lava rather than large explosions is what defines an effusive eruption.

items.prompt: Iceland's Laki eruption of 1783–1784 poured out lava rather than exploding. How did it affect Iceland?

options.label: It killed about a fifth of the population
No one died, since the lava moved slowly
It harmed only a few farms near the vent
It closed harbours but caused no deaths

items.explain: Laki produced about 15 km³ of lava and killed one fifth of Iceland's people, showing effusive eruptions can be as dangerous as explosive ones.

items.prompt: A volcano's magma is thick, sticky and full of dissolved water vapour and carbon dioxide. What eruption style does it most likely produce?

options.label: A steady flow of runny lava
A sudden explosive blast
A slow lava lake that never spills
Quiet steam with no rock at all

items.explain: Explosive eruptions usually involve thick, viscous magma high in gases, and the sudden release of that gas drives the blast.

items.prompt: Geologists believe many huge ancient eruptions are missing from their records. Why is the size of so many unknown?

options.label: Eruptions before humans were all small
Scientists count only eruptions people wrote about
Old ash always dissolves within a few years
Erosion and moving plates wiped out the evidence

items.explain: Erosion and plate tectonics have destroyed much of the record, so many eruptions did not leave enough evidence to measure.

items.prompt: Enormous flood-basalt eruptions in the deep past are often linked with what other event in Earth's history?

options.label: The start of every ice age
Supercontinents breaking apart
Large asteroid impacts on land
The first forests spreading

items.explain: Flood basalts from large igneous provinces are often associated with the breakup of supercontinents such as Pangea.

items.prompt: People have lived through many kinds of eruptions. What kind has never happened on a large scale in human history?

options.label: An explosive eruption throwing out ash
An effusive lava eruption in Iceland
A flood-basalt eruption
An eruption lasting decades

items.explain: No large flood-basalt eruptions have happened in human history; the most recent was over 10 million years ago.
